extracted.intended_audience: PRSA members and public relations professionals
extracted.subtask_description: The PRSA Code of Ethics sets core professional values, provisions of conduct, and topic-specific advisories that govern ethical practice in public relations and guide member behavior across communications activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: We serve the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for those we represent. We provide a voice in the marketplace of ideas, facts, and viewpoints to aid informed public debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle establishes duty to represent clients responsibly while considering the public interest and contributing to informed debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: We adhere to the highest standards of accuracy and truth in advancing the interests of those we represent and in communicating with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires accuracy, truthfulness and avoidance of deception across all communications and representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: We acquire and responsibly use specialized knowledge and experience. We advance the profession through continued professional development, research, and education. We build mutual understanding, credibility, and relationships among a wide array of institutions and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligates continuing professional development, responsible use of specialized knowledge, and educating others to maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide objective counsel to those we represent. We are accountable for our actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires objective advice and accountability; avoid actions that compromise independent judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: We are faithful to those we represent, while honoring our obligation to serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance duty to clients/employers with broader public interest obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: We deal fairly with clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, the media, and the general public. We respect all opinions and support the right of free expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligates equitable treatment of stakeholders and respect for free expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free Flow of Information (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Protecting and advancing the free flow of accurate and truthful information is essential to serving the public interest and contributing to informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: maintain integrity of relationships with media, government officials, and public; aid informed decision-making. Guidelines: preserve integrity of communication process; be honest and accurate; act promptly to correct errors; ensure gifts are nominal/legal/infrequent so free flow is preserved. Examples of improper conduct: giving expensive gifts to influence coverage; entertaining officials beyond legal limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Promoting healthy and fair competition among professionals preserves an ethical climate while fostering a robust business environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: promote respect and fair competition and serve public interest by providing choice. Guidelines: follow ethical hiring practices that respect open competition; preserve intellectual property rights. Examples of improper conduct: sharing helpful information with a competing firm during a pitch; spreading malicious rumors to recruit talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Information (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Open communication fosters informed decision making in a democratic society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: build trust by revealing information needed for responsible decision-making. Guidelines: be honest and accurate; promptly correct erroneous communications; investigate truthfulness of released information; reveal sponsors and financial interests; avoid deceptive practices. Examples of improper conduct: creating front groups; lying by omission about financials; not correcting inaccurate information; using people posing as volunteers in campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguarding Confidences (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Client trust requires appropriate protection of confidential and private information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: protect privacy rights of clients, organizations and individuals. Guidelines: safeguard confidences of present/former/prospective clients and employees; protect privileged or insider information; advise authorities if confidential information is being divulged. Examples of improper conduct: taking confidential information to a new job and using it; intentionally leaking proprietary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of Interest (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Avoiding real, potential or perceived conflicts of interest builds the trust of clients, employers, and the publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: earn trust by avoiding situations that conflict with society's interests. Guidelines: act in best interest of client/employer (even subordinate personal interests); avoid actions/circumstances that appear to compromise judgement; disclose promptly any existing or potential conflicts; encourage clients to assess conflicts after notification. Examples: failing to disclose financial interest in a client's competitor; representing a competing company without informing prospective client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancing the Profession (Provision of Conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Principle: Public relations professionals work constantly to strengthen the public’s trust in the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent: build respect and credibility, improve and adapt practices. Guidelines: acknowledge obligation to protect/enhance profession; stay informed and pursue professional development; decline representation that requires actions contrary to the Code; accurately define PR activities; counsel and require subordinates to adhere to Code; report noncompliant practices. Examples: publicly declaring a product safe without disclosing contrary evidence; assigning questionable client work to non-members to avoid membership obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Standards Advisories (ESAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: BEPS issues Ethical Standards Advisories to provide guidance within the framework of the Code; ESAs are informational and not legal advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESAs offer topic-specific guidance (e.g., misinformation ESA). A complete list is available to members on MyPRSA. Use ESAs to interpret and apply Code provisions in evolving situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-for-Play
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: when payment is required for development and publishing of content (print or digital) as a quid pro quo for coverage or visibility; this practice can deceive consumers by hiding the paid nature of content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position: Pay-for-play conflicts with PRSA Code (Free Flow of Information, Disclosure, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession) and values (Honesty, Fairness, Independence). Recommendations: request and include disclosure when compensation provided for exposure; encourage disclosure of non-monetary items (travel, gifts); always encourage clear disclosure of crucial information to consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics & Social Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media’s speed, frequency and reach create new ethical challenges requiring PR practitioners to adopt a higher standard of practice consistent with the PRSA Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code provisions addressing social media include Disclosure of Information, Safeguarding Confidences, Conflicts of Interest, and Enhancing the Profession. Recommendations: fully disclose paid placements and associations per medium and FTC guidance; protect confidential information; be aware of employee free-speech rights (NLRB); disclose conflicts of interest when communicating; require influencer disclosures and ensure gifts are nominal/legal/infrequent; use social media to inform publics and share best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism is unauthorized use or close imitation of another's language or thoughts and representing them as one's own; it can be intentional or inadvertent and may be treated as fraud or theft of intellectual property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position: Even inadvertent plagiarism carries equal weight to intentional misrepresentation. Relevant Code provisions: Free Flow of Information, Competition, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest; values implicated include Honesty, Expertise, Fairness. Recommendations: do not copy content even if edited; use your own words and paraphrase with credit; when paraphrasing give credit; use quotation marks and credit when copying exact wording; disclose all sources and obtain permissions or pay licensing when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid Spokespersons and Influencers
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone paid to serve as a spokesperson, advocate or influencer for an organization must disclose the contractual arrangement or relationship providing compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant Code provisions: Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Professional values implicated: Advocacy, Independence, Honesty, Fairness. Recommendations: disclose commercial relationships in advance or simultaneous with the public forum; every party in the contractual relationship must disclose; be honest and accurate about sponsors and financial interests; failure to disclose is improper conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing Front Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Front groups are organizations created or labeled to mislead the public about their true mission; assisting front groups constitutes deception by hiding true intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position: Assisting front groups violates the Code and should be avoided even if lawfully permissible. Relevant provisions: Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession. Values implicated: Honesty, Fairness, Advocacy. Recommendation: refuse to assist efforts that mislead or hide sponsorship or intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overstating Fees or Compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging clients for services not performed or overstating hours/fees undermines trust and harms the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position: Members should charge only for services rendered and in accordance with contracts. Relevant provision: Enhancing the Profession; values: Honesty. Recommendations: report services rendered, time and out-of-pocket charges accurately; avoid inflating charges or support data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native Advertising & Sponsored Content
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear distinction between organic content and sponsored/native advertising must be made apparent to consumers; sponsors should be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant provisions: Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Competition, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession; values: Honesty, Advocacy, Fairness. Recommendations: ensure sponsorship is fully disclosed within the content context; disclosures should be clear and appropriate to the medium; sponsored content must be easily distinguishable from organic content and not attempt to deceive consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI and Leadership Accountabilities (Machine Learning Accountabilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: As AI/ML makes decisions formerly made by humans, accountability for errant decisions should rest with human beings with oversight responsibility at the time the decision is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position: It is not satisfactory to blame machines; organizations and leaders with oversight must identify root causes and corrective actions with transparency. Relevant Code provisions: Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession; values: Honesty, Advocacy, Fairness. Recommendations: counsel leadership that humans hold accountability; draw clear lines of human responsibility when developing communications involving AI; present those lines forthrightly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media as a Reflection of Majority Opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media activity is not a scientifically vetted indicator of majority public opinion; a small fraction of users often drives most activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position: Communicators should not present social media as an accurate measure of majority sentiment. Relevant provisions: Free Flow of Information, Disclosure of Information, Enhancing the Profession; values: Honesty, Fairness, Advocacy. Recommendations: when sharing analysis based on social media, remind audiences the source is informal and may not represent broader public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Leaks
rubrics_metrics.description: Members should refrain from leaking confidential or proprietary information to media or stakeholders without expressed approval of organization leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position: Leaking undermines trust and may be illegal. Relevant provisions: Safeguarding Confidences, Disclosure of Information, Free Flow of Information, Conflicts of Interest, Enhancing the Profession; values: Loyalty, Honesty, Fairness, Advocacy. Recommendations: be aware of laws/regulations/contracts governing information flow; adhere to contractual and legal obligations; never autonomously share confidential information; follow procedures for approving disclosures.
